rounds.text: Sanjivani Paranteral Ltd demonstrates superior capital efficiency through a Return on Assets of 8.48%, comfortably outperforming the sector benchmark of 6.38% [E8]. Market pricing currently rests at a modest ₹ 167 with a market capitalization of ₹ 205 Cr [E2, E3], sitting at just 35% of its 52-week range [E5] despite powerful operational momentum including 33% year-on-year sales growth [E47] and profit growth exceeding 20% year-on-year [E50]. This recent acceleration is starting to outpace expectations, with profit growth exceeding one-year price growth by 17% [E41]. Long-term shareholders have been rewarded with a compounded share price growth of 44% over 5 years and 26% over 10 years [E16, E17]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth stands at -8% alongside a 4% compounded sales growth rate [E14, E15], and the one-year share price growth is -25% [E19].

Sanjivani Paranteral Ltd trades at a rich price-to-book multiple of 4.37x which sits notably higher than its sector benchmark of 3.13x [E7]. This premium asset valuation is completely disconnected from the actual fundamentals of the business, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth that has contracted by -8% [E15]. Furthermore, the top-line expansion is sluggish, with compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months registering at a meager 4% [E14]. Investors are therefore paying an inflated price for a business whose growth engine is visibly stalling. The market has already begun to recognize this underlying deterioration, punishing the stock with a 1-year compounded share price growth of -25% [E19]. Conceded: the company displays a healthy return on assets of 8.48% compared to the sector benchmark of 6.38% [E8].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth has contracted by -8% [E15], and compounded sales growth over the same period is 4% [E14]. However, the bear focuses excessively on a single lagging snapshot while ignoring powerful momentum signals showing sales up 33% year-over-year [E47] alongside strong overall sales growth [E48]. Furthermore, profit growth exceeding 20% year-over-year [E50] directly contradicts the notion of a stalling growth engine. Finally, the higher price-to-book multiple of 4.37x [E7] is justified by a superior return on assets of 8.48% that outperforms the sector benchmark of 6.38% [E8].
